q: The minimum value of 2sin 2 θ + 3cos 2 θ is ?

q: If $${\left( {r\cos \theta - \sqrt 3 } \right)^2}$$ + $${\left( {r\sin \theta - 1} \right)^2}$$ = 0, then the value of $$\frac{{r\tan \theta + \sec \theta }}{{r\sec \theta + \tan \theta }}$$ is equal to?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\left( {r\cos \theta - \sqrt 3 } \right)^2} + {\left( {r\sin \theta - 1} \right)^2} = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {r\cos \theta - \sqrt 3 } \right)^2} = 0,{\text{ }}{\left( {r\sin \theta - 1} \right)^2} = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow r{\text{ cos}}\theta = \sqrt 3 ........(i) \\ & \Rightarrow r\sin \theta = 1.........(ii) \\ & {\text{Squaring and adding equation (i) and (ii)}} \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2}{\cos ^2}\theta + {r^2}{\sin ^2}\theta = 3 + 1 \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2}\left( {{\text{co}}{{\text{s}}^2}\theta + {{\sin }^2}\theta } \right) = 4 \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2} = 4 \\ & \Rightarrow r = 2 \\ & {\text{tan}}\theta = \frac{{r\sin \theta }}{{r{\text{ cos}}\theta }} = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}{\text{ and }}r{\text{ cos}}\theta = \sqrt 3 \\ & \cos \theta = \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{r}, \\ & \sec \theta = \frac{r}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \frac{{r\tan \theta + \sec \theta }}{{r\sec \theta + \tan \theta }} \\ & = \frac{{\frac{r}{{\sqrt 3 }} + \frac{r}{{\sqrt 3 }}}}{{\frac{{{r^2}}}{{\sqrt 3 }} + \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}}} \\ & = \frac{{r\left( {\frac{2}{{\sqrt 3 }}} \right)}}{{\frac{{{r^2} + 1}}{{\sqrt 3 }}}} \\ & = \frac{{2r}}{{{r^2} + 1}} \\ & = \frac{{2 \times 2}}{{{2^2} + 1}} \\ & = \frac{4}{5} \\ & \\ & {\bf{Alternate:}} \\ & r = 2 \\ & {\text{tan}}\theta = \frac{{r\sin \theta }}{{r{\text{ cos}}\theta }} = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} \\ & \theta = {30^ \circ } \\ & = \frac{{2\tan {{30}^ \circ } + \sec {{30}^ \circ }}}{{2\sec {{30}^ \circ } + \tan {{30}^ \circ }}} \\ & = \frac{{2 \times \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }} + \frac{2}{{\sqrt 3 }}}}{{2 \times \frac{2}{{\sqrt 3 }} + \frac{1}{{\sqrt 3 }}}} \\ & = \frac{4}{5} \end{aligned}$$

q: sin 2 5° + sin 2 10° + sin 2 15° + ...... sin 2 85° + sin 2 90° is equal to?
s: Given, (sin 2 5° + sin 2 10° + sin 2 15° + . . . . . . + sin 2 85° ) + sin 2 90° We know that sinθ = cos(90° - θ ) Therefore sin 2 85° = cos 2 (90° - 85°) = cos 2 5° Similary sin 2 60° = cos 2 (90° - 60°) = cos 2 40° And we also know that sin 2 θ + cos 2 θ = 1 There are 8 pair in given equation sin 2 5° + cos 2 5° = 1 sin 2 10° + cos 2 10° = 1 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . sin 2 40° + cos 2 40° = 1 i.e. 8 + sin 2 45° + sin 2 90° ⇒ 8 + $$\frac{1}{2}$$ + 1 = $$9\frac{1}{2}$$ Short Trick: $$\left( {si{n^2}{5^ \circ }\, + \,{{\sin }^2}{{10}^ \circ }\, + \,{{\sin }^2}{{15}^ \circ }\, + \,.....\,{{\sin }^2}{{85}^ \circ }} \right)\, +$$ $$\,{\sin ^2}90$$ $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Number of terms}} \\ & = \left\{ {\left( {\frac{{85 - 5}}{5}} \right) + 1} \right\}{\text{ + 1}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\frac{{17}}{2}{\text{ + 1}} \\ & {\text{Sum of series}} = 9\frac{1}{2} \end{aligned}$$

s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{sin A}} - \cos {\text{A}} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{2} \\ & {\bf{Shortcut \,\,method:}} \\ & {\text{Put, }}\theta = {60^ \circ } \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{sin A}} - \cos {\text{A}} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{sin }}{60^ \circ } - \cos {60^ \circ } = \frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{2} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{2}({\text{Matched}}) \\ & Hence, \\ & {\text{sin A}}.cos{\text{A}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4} \\ & \\ & {\bf{Alternate:}} \\ & {\text{sin A}} - \cos {\text{A}} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{2} \\ & {\text{Squaring both side,}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{ si}}{{\text{n}}^2}{\text{ A + }}{\cos ^2}{\text{A}} - {\text{2}}{\text{.sin A}}.cos{\text{A}} = {\left( {\frac{{\sqrt 3 - 1}}{2}} \right)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 1 - 2{\text{sin A}}.cos{\text{A = }}\frac{{3 + 1 - 2\sqrt 3 }}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow 2{\text{sin A}}.cos{\text{A}} = 1 - 2\frac{{\left( {2 - \sqrt 3 } \right)}}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow 2{\text{sin A}}.cos{\text{A}} = \frac{{2 - 2 + \sqrt 3 }}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow {\text{sin A}}.cos{\text{A}} = \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4} \end{aligned}$$

q: $$\frac{{\sin \theta + \cos \theta }}{{{\text{sin}}\theta - \cos \theta }} = 3,$$ then the value of $${\sin ^4}\theta - {\text{co}}{{\text{s}}^4}\theta$$ is?
s: If in the any question componendo and dividendo already used as $$\frac{{a + b}}{{a - b}} = \frac{m}{n}$$ If second time you also want to apply componendo dividendo rule then result will be $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{a}{b} = \frac{{m + n}}{{m - n}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{\sin \theta + \cos \theta }}{{{\text{sin}}\theta - \cos \theta }} = 3 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \sin \theta + {\text{cos}}\theta = 3\sin \theta - 3{\text{cos}}\theta \\ & \Leftrightarrow 2\sin \theta = 4{\text{cos}}\theta \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{{\sin \theta }}{{{\text{cos}}\theta }} = \frac{2}{1} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\text{tan}}\theta = \frac{2}{1} = \frac{{\text{P}}}{{\text{B}}} \\ & \left[ {\therefore {\text{sin}}\theta = \frac{{\text{P}}}{{\text{H}}} = \frac{2}{{\sqrt 5 }}{\text{ and cos}}\theta = \frac{{\text{B}}}{{\text{H}}} = \frac{1}{{\sqrt 5 }}} \right] \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow {\sin ^4}\theta - {\text{co}}{{\text{s}}^4}\theta \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {{{\sin }^2}\theta + {\text{co}}{{\text{s}}^2}\theta } \right)\left( {{{\sin }^2}\theta - {\text{co}}{{\text{s}}^2}\theta } \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow 1\left( {{{\sin }^2}\theta - {\text{co}}{{\text{s}}^2}\theta } \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\left( {\frac{2}{{\sqrt 5 }}} \right)^2} - {\left( {\frac{1}{{\sqrt 5 }}} \right)^2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{4}{5} - \frac{1}{5} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{3}{5} \end{aligned}$$
